content:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: automated alert: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (model-profile: int8-prod-2026). p99=3.2s, baseline SLO p99=0.9s. paging oncall.
sam: paging @oncall — I'm grabbing it.
katie: seeing same in graphs. p95 up to 1.1s, p99 jump to 3s, tail distribution shows long right tail. Streaming stalls visible: token generation stalls at kv fetch during expansion windows.
avi: (typo check) no change
avi (sre): tagging for visibility — possible quantization fallout after yesterday's profile rollout to int8-prod-2026.
avi: any deploys in the last 24h? deploy-bot: recent rollout: redwood-gptx-int8-2026 rolled to 60% traffic at 02:10 UTC (yesterday).
avi: thanks. can we roll back quick if needed?
sam: first step: enable routing to fallback fp16 variant for canary customers. k8s route change queued.
chris: pushing a config patch to routing service now. command:
```
PATCH /routes/streaming
{ "fallback_profile": "fp16-stable-2025", "traffic_shift": 0.2 }
```
maya: running a targeted warm-up on fp16 pool for affected region (us-west-2) to avoid cold-start latency.
avi: logs from serving nodes show these stack traces during stalls:
```
E 03:14:02.342 kernel_executor.cpp  warn: kv_cache_miss -> blocking fetch
W 03:14:02.347 quant_calib.cpp    error: dequant path slow: row-lock wait 47ms
```
avi: that wait on row-lock in quant_calib looks suspicious.
avi: correlating with APM traces — tail spikes map to calibration cache flush events triggered by new weight layout for int8.
katie: are we seeing increased contention on KV backend? I/O wait looks low, CPU is spiking on certain hosts with many long-tail requests.
avi: hypothesis: new int8 profile introduced a calibration step for certain sequence lengths that invalidates prefix KVs and forces synchronous recomputation for a subset of requests.
sam: mitigation plan sketch:
- immediate: route 40% of traffic to fp16-stable in affected region (reduces exposure)
- temporary: throttle long-seq requests (>1024 tokens) to avoid hitting the recalib path
- short-term: patch serving runtime to make calibration async with best-effort fallback
- follow-up: revert int8 profile rollout if p99 doesn't improve in 20m
chris: routing patch applied — traffic shift +40% to fp16 in us-west-2. confirm metrics.
katie: metrics after shift: p99 down from 3.2s -> 1.4s at 03:22 UTC. still above SLO but greatly improved. p95 stable at ~0.95s.
maya: customer-impact check: eva-cs, can you validate top customers in us-west-2?
eva-cs: checking support dashboard — two accounts reported degraded streaming quality starting ~02:50 UTC. both on canary plan. no paid-enterprise alerts yet. I'm opening CS tickets and notifying customers of active mitigation.
sam: starting oncall handoff note — if we need to escalate to infra, I'll page infra after this first rotation.
avi: digging deeper — grabbing heap/profile dumps from affected process to check for lock contention patterns.
chris: can we temporarily disable the calibration step via config flag? I see a flag in runtime: `--synchronous-calib=false` toggles behavior.
sam: toggled `--synchronous-calib=false` on two worst hosts. restart triggered via orchestrator. watch pods.
katie: after toggle and routing shift, p99 now at 0.95s at 03:30 UTC — back within SLO. streaming stalls mostly gone.
sam: great. for now keep route shift and flag toggle until we have a durable fix.
maya: creating follow-up ticket for ML/Runtime: need root-cause and safer rollout gating for precision changes (alerts on KV invalidation events, canary ramp rules to avoid synchronous calib on warm traffic).
avi: capturing traces and logs, will attach to ticket. interestingly, requests with many short prefixes didn't hit the problem; it's specific to long prepopulated KV states.
chris: send me the exact shard IDs of the affected hosts so infra can check kernel scheduling and lock stats.
katie: adding postmortem owners: sam (oncall), avi (ML eng), chris (runtime), maya (cs liaison).
avi: temporary mitigation: maintain routing fallback + async calib flag OFF for 2 hours, then try a controlled re-roll to 10% with instrumentation.
eva-cs: notifying affected customers that mitigation is live and we'll follow up with root-cause + ETA for permanent fix.
sam: oncall handover in 30m — I'll leave a summary in #incidents-ops:
- incident id: 2156789012
- detection: automated p99 alert 03:12 UTC
- impact: p99 spike to 3.2s, streaming stalls for long-seq requests, two customer reports
- mitigations: routed 40% traffic to fp16; toggled async calib flag; p99 back to ~0.95s
- next actions: ML to investigate calibration invalidation logic; runtime to add guardrails; follow-up postmortem
maya: thanks team. closing paging unless we see regression. will coordinate postmortem and CS comms.
